extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and policymakers interested in post‑war international affairs
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper report reproducing and explaining the Moscow communique of the Big Three foreign ministers (U.S., U.K., USSR) describing agreed postwar arrangements for Japan, Korea, atomic control, and recognition/conditions for Romania and Bulgaria. The page combines reportage and large quoted blocks of the official communique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of an Allied Council for Japan
rubrics_metrics.description: "There shall be established an Allied Council with its seat in Tokyo."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council created to consult with and advise the supreme commander on carrying out surrender terms, occupation and control of Japan; its policy recommendations flow from the Far Eastern Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allied Council composition and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The council will be represented by four nations: the United States, Russia, Great Britain and China; the fourth seat jointly represents Britain, Australia, New Zealand and India.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: China's concurrence was required. Russia's inclusion increases participation in the Far Eastern deliberations; the fourth seat may represent a grouping (Britain+Dominions+India) rather than a single state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allied Council meetings and staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Allied Council shall meet not less often than once every two weeks."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each member shall be entitled to have an appropriate staff consisting of military and civilian advisers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allied Council scope and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The council will "respect existing control machinery in Japan" and "shall not make recommendations with regard to the conduct of military operations nor with regard to territorial adjustments."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The council's role is consultative and policy‑shaping rather than operational or territorial‑settling; it advises the supreme commander and the Far Eastern Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supreme commander (MacArthur) — executive authority and consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: The supreme commander is "the sole executive authority for the Allied powers in Japan." He "will consult and advise with the council in advance of the issuance of orders on matters of substance, the exigencies of the situation permitting. His decisions upon these matters shall be controlling."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the council advises and is consulted on matters of substance, the supreme commander's decisions are binding; consultation is expected when practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supreme commander emergency powers
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases of necessity the Supreme Commander may make decisions concerning the change of individual ministers of the Japanese government and filling of cabinet vacancies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such emergency decisions are permitted after appropriate preliminary consultation with representatives of other Allied powers when practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission review of supreme commander's directives
rubrics_metrics.description: The commission would have the authority "to review, on the request of any member, any directive issued to MacArthur or by any action taken by him 'involving policy decisions within the jurisdiction of the commission.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review power provides a check: the commission serves as an advisory body whose policy decisions are carried out by the supreme commander, but those actions can be reviewed if contested by members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Far Eastern Commission — membership and enlargement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Far Eastern Commission is an international body whose membership may be increased by agreement among participating powers; it will provide for consultations with United Nations representatives and may include representatives of other United Nations members having territories in the Far East.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commission can expand as conditions warrant; it provides policy recommendations for Japan and coordinates with UN representatives on matters of particular concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Far Eastern Commission — functional limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The commission "shall not make recommendations with regard to the conduct of military operations nor with regard to territorial adjustments."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commission's remit is political/administrative policy for occupation and reconstruction, not operational military command or decisions on territorial boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Far Eastern Commission voting pattern / high‑power veto
rubrics_metrics.description: The pattern for the new Far Eastern commission contemplates high‑power veto rights; the commission could take action by less than a unanimous vote only if the United States, Britain, Russia, China and two more of the 11 members agreed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice this means the major powers retain effective blocking power over major policy changes; the U.S. could block decisions on Japan with which it disagreed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and remit of an Atomic Energy Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: A commission is to be established by the General Assembly to consider problems arising from the discovery of atomic energy and related matters; it shall submit reports and recommendations to the Security Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commission is charged to proceed with utmost dispatch and to inquire into all phases of the problem, making specific proposals and recommendations to ensure peaceful uses and international safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic Commission — relations with UN organs and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: The commission shall submit its reports and recommendations to the Security Council; "the Security Council shall issue directions to the commission in matters affecting security" and the commission shall be accountable to the Security Council on security matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On security matters the Security Council has primacy; the commission's reports may be transmitted by the Security Council to the General Assembly and other UN organs as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic Commission — composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The commission shall be composed of one representative from each of those states represented on the Security Council, and Canada when that state is not a member of the Security Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each representative may have such assistants as he may desire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic Commission — rules of procedure and staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: The commission shall have whatever staff it may deem necessary, and shall make recommendations for its rules of procedure to the Security Council, which shall approve them as a procedural matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational details (staffing, internal procedures) are for the commission to propose and for the Security Council to approve procedurally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic Commission terms of reference — exchange of scientific information
rubrics_metrics.description: "(A) For extending between all nations the exchange of basic scientific information for peaceful ends;"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote open scientific exchange related to peaceful applications of atomic discoveries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic Commission terms of reference — control of atomic energy
rubrics_metrics.description: "(B) For control of atomic energy to the extent necessary to insure its use only for peaceful purposes;"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design controls to prevent military/weapon use while permitting peaceful development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic Commission terms of reference — elimination of atomic and mass‑destruction weapons
rubrics_metrics.description: "(C) For the elimination from national armaments of atomic weapons and of all other major weapons adaptable to mass destruction;"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for disarmament of atomic and analogous mass‑destruction weapons as part of commission proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic Commission terms of reference — safeguards and inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: "(D) For effective safeguards by way of inspection and other means to protect complying states against the hazards of violations and evasions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design inspection/safeguard regimes to protect compliant states from others' violations and ensure confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic Commission — staged approach and confidence building
rubrics_metrics.description: Work should proceed by separate stages, the successful completion of each of which will develop the necessary confidence of the world before the next stage is undertaken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A phased implementation is advised to build international trust before moving to more sensitive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Korea — provisional government and joint commission
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional Korean democratic government shall be set up; a joint commission of representatives of the United States command in southern Korea and the Soviet command in northern Korea will be established to assist formation and prepare proposals, consulting with Korean democratic parties and social organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations of the joint commission shall be presented to the governments of the US, USSR, UK and China prior to final decisions by the two governments directly represented on the joint commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Korea — trusteeship and ultimate aim
rubrics_metrics.description: The commission is to work out measures for helping and assisting (trusteeship) the political, economic and social progress of the Korean people; consultation about a five‑year trusteeship is to be submitted to the four governments, with the ultimate aim of reestablishment of Korea as an independent state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trusteeship proposed for up to five years to prepare Korea for independent, democratic self‑government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Korea — urgent coordination between US and Soviet commands
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish permanent coordination in administrative‑economic matters between the United States command in southern Korea and the Soviet command in northern Korea, a conference of representatives of the United States and Soviet commands shall be convened within two weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate administrative and economic coordination is mandated to address urgent problems affecting both zones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Romania — government broadening and recognition conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The reorganized Romanian government should include one member of the National Peasant party and one member of the Liberal party; the commission shall satisfy itself they are truly representative and suitable; the reorganized government should declare that free and unfettered elections will be held as soon as possible on the basis of universal and secret ballot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition by the United States and United Kingdom is conditioned on inclusion of adequate party representation, assurances of freedoms (press, speech, religion, association) and commitment to free elections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bulgaria — advice on inclusion and recognition conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Soviet government will advise Bulgaria on inclusion in its government of the Fatherland Front plus two additional representatives of other democratic groups who are truly representative and suitable; when the US and UK are convinced the advice has been accepted and additional representatives included the US and UK will recognize the Bulgarian government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition is contingent on demonstrable inclusion of broader democratic representation and satisfactory assurances from the Bulgarian government.

rubrics_metrics.name: General commissions — representatives' assistants and staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Each representative on commissions may have such assistants as he may desire; commissions shall have whatever staff they deem necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissions are expected to provide adequate staffing (civilian and military advisers where relevant) to carry out their mandates.
